newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE TAKES POLE FOR SAN MARINO GRAND PRIX.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE TAKES POLE FOR SAN MARINO GRAND PRIX.

text.p: World championship leader Jacques Villeneuve broke the qualifying lap record at the Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari by more than three seconds on Saturday when he secured pole position for Sunday's San Marino Grand Prix.

Canadian Villeneuve, 26, driving a Renault-powered Williams, clocked a time of one minute and 23.303 seconds at the famous circuit in Ferrari's heartland -- where his father Gilles's feats for the Italian team are cherished -- for his fourth successive pole position of the season.

It was his fifth successive, including last year's season-ending Japanese Grand Prix, and ensured he will start the 62-lap race as favourite to win and retain his early grip on the drivers' championship.

Villeneuve's time was good enough to leave him 0.3 seconds ahead of nearest rival and Williams team mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen of Germany, who also smashed the previous best lap at the track recorded by Michael Schumacher in a Ferrari last year.

Schumacher was third fastest on a day when the top five drivers were separated by only 0.7 seconds. Frenchman Olivier Panis in a Prost -- the leading Bridgestone-tyred car among the Goodyear-dominated field -- took fourth place ahead of Ralf Schumacher in a Jordan.

Italian Giancarlo Fisichella, Ralf's team mate who came off worse from their crash in the Argentine Grand Prix two weeks ago, took sixth place in the second Jordan. The pair have barely spoken and the accident ended their friendship, said Fisichella.

Briton Eddie Irvine, who was fastest for Ferrari in Friday's opening practice, slipped to ninth and the two Benettons of Austrian Gerhard Berger and Frenchman Jean Alesi to 11th and 14th, after frustration with their set-up.

Villeneuve remains clear favourite and said he felt confident of competing well. "It was tight and stressful in the session, but more fun on the track than it used to be. The grip of the tyres is amazing," said Villeneuve.

"But, as you could see in Argentina, we are now very close to the edge of the performance of the tyres and so, I think, race strategy is going to be very important. However, I am happier with my race set-up than my qualifying set-up so I am confident."

After Friday's warm sunshine, Saturday's session was run in cool, but dry conditions with the red-capped Ferrari fans among the big crowd hoping for a repeat of their team's domination of opening practice.

Michael Schumacher threatened to deliver for them early in the session when he topped the times ahead of Villeneuve before both were eclipsed by the pace of Frentzen 20 minutes into the one-hour session.
Schumacher, senior, showed he was not finished after 28 minutes when he pushed Villeneuve out of second place as the leading drivers traded close times.

Then, after half an hour, Villeneuve stamped his authority on the proceedings with a lap in 1:23.586. This left him one-tenth clear of Frentzen with Michael Schumacher third and his younger brother Ralf fourth.

Incredibly, 19 of the 22 runners in qualifying clocked times that were inside Schumacher's 1996 pole lap -- evidence that the 'tyre war' between Goodyear and Bridgestone has caused a leap in speed this season.
